The [[Copa América]] is an international [[association football]] competition established in 1916.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://biblioteca.afa.org.ar/libros/libro_84/ |title=X Campeonato Sud Americano de Football |publisher=biblioteca.afa.org.ar |access-date=27 February 2015}}</ref><ref name="CopaAmericaOldestContTournament">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/en/content/oldest-continental-tournament-world|title=The oldest main continental tournament in the world|publisher=CONMEBOL|access-date=3 April 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221011523/http://www.conmebol.com/en/content/oldest-continental-tournament-world|archive-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> It is contested by the [[List of men's national association football teams#CONMEBOL (South America)|men's national teams]] of the members of the [[CONMEBOL|Confederación Sudamericana de Fútbol]] (CONMEBOL), the sport's continental governing body.

Early editions of the tournament, then known as the South American Football Championship, consisted of a [[round-robin tournament|round-robin]] group, where the team with the most points was declared the champion (with a [[one-game playoff|play-off]] to break a tie if necessary). In 1975, when the tournament was rebranded to its current title, a final stage using the [[Single-elimination tournament|single-elimination format]] was introduced, which culminates with a [[Final (competition)|final match]] between the last two teams remaining in contention. This type of format has been used ever since, except in 1989 and 1991, which featured a final group stage.

[[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] defeated [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]] in [[2024 Copa América final|the final]] of the latest competition, held in 2024.
